commit.message:
measurement/week-4-review: add leadership sharing template

Reviewer (Jen, Head of Product): reviewing her own PM pilot results
is only half the value — she needs to write it up for her skip-level.
Doc ended at 'here's what you learned' with no on-ramp to the
conversation she actually has to have on Monday.

Added: a copy-paste email template covering tl;dr, what ran, what
changed in decisions, what broke, what surprised, next actions, cost
posture, and security posture. Designed to be edited in 10 min.

sample-yaml: warn against always_allow as first-deploy default

Reviewer (Marcus, staff eng): the example YAML had
permission_policy.type: always_allow. Convenient, but unsafe as a
starter default for any write-capable agent in production. Readers
would copy it verbatim and learn the hard way.

Added: inline comment block explicitly warning against always_allow
for first 4 weeks, recommending ask_for_confirmation or
allow_with_rate_limit instead, and positioning always_allow as an
after-audit upgrade, not a starter.

cowork/02-local-brief: add Windows paths for Obsidian/Logseq

Reviewer (Kiran, doc nitpicker): Obsidian/Bear/Logseq paths were all
macOS. Windows readers had to translate, which is where typos and
path errors live.

Added: parallel Windows path block for Obsidian (local + OneDrive
vault) and Logseq, plus a note that Claude Desktop normalizes forward
slashes — so the prompt itself stays platform-agnostic.

cowork/01-transcript: cloud folder sync + file size guidance

Reviewer 1 (Priya, APM): transcripts live in Google Drive, not local
~/Documents. Task as written doesn't work for her workflow.
Reviewer 2 (Marcus, staff eng): no guidance on file size — a 50MB
audio file in the folder would timeout the task silently.

Added: (1) two options for cloud-stored transcripts — desktop sync
client (recommended) or Managed Agent alternative with Google Drive
MCP; (2) file size guidance (under 100KB works cleanly, 100KB-1MB
slower, over 1MB needs a size filter in the prompt).

engineer-handoff-brief: add common PM misconceptions table

Reviewer (Marcus, staff eng): hand-off briefs usually leave engineers
ambushed by PM assumptions mid-project. Better to surface the common
ones up front in the kickoff.

Added: 5-row misconceptions table covering (1) prompt ~= 30% of work,
(2) YAML paste isn't deployment, (3) security review is not a rubber
stamp, (4) prompts decay and need tuning cadence, (5) bounded
hallucination is not zero hallucination. Positioned as a 10-min
kickoff conversation that saves 2 weeks of expectation-mismatch.

managed-agents/03-transcript: explain 3 transcript input mechanisms

Reviewer (Sam, skeptic engineer): 'receives a meeting transcript' —
how? No answer. Agent looks magical but the input pipe is the
unsolved engineering problem.

Added: 3-mechanism table (Otter/Fireflies webhook, Zoom cloud+script,
manual Slack channel upload) with setup effort for each, plus a
pointer to the Cowork transcript task as the alternative if you
don't record meetings today.

managed-agents/01-support: clarify starter (web) vs upgrade (MCP) path

Reviewer (Marcus, staff eng): unclear whether this agent reads
Zendesk/Intercom tickets or does web search. The prompt mentioned
forum posts which suggested web, but the 'hand to engineer' framing
suggested MCP wiring. Ambiguity was costing buy-in.

Added: explicit starter-vs-upgrade framing — starter uses web
browsing (30 min PM solo setup), upgrade adds Zendesk/Intercom MCP
(~1 day eng work). Picks by use case: consumer products get enough
signal from web, enterprise products under NDA need the MCP upgrade.

routines/02-morning-brief: top-5 meeting cap for busy days

Reviewer (Priya, APM): on a 10-meeting day the Slack DM was too long
to read on phone. The brief became useless at exactly the moment it
was most needed.

Added: priority-ranked capping logic — external customer calls and
manager 1:1s rank highest; top 5 get full briefings, rest get a
one-line list at the bottom. Keeps the DM scannable.

appendix-connector-ids: web path for Slack IDs, real URL examples

Reviewer 1 (Priya, APM): Slack ID instructions assumed desktop app.
Half of readers use Slack in-browser and couldn't find the ID.
Reviewer 2 (Kiran, doc nitpicker): Notion page vs database URL
distinction was abstract. Needed concrete examples to copy-compare.

Added: (1) web-based Slack channel ID path via URL extraction, (2)
concrete page URL + database URL examples with the ?v= distinction,
(3) guidance on when to use each URL type.

team-rollout: add 8-week slow variant and pushback response table

Reviewer 1 (Rohan, senior PM): 4-week rollout too aggressive for
change-averse orgs. No on-ramp for PMs already at capacity.
Reviewer 2 (Jen, Head of Product): no guidance on the pushback I'll
actually hear from my PMs.

Added: (1) 8-week slower variant where you pilot yourself first,
then 2 volunteers, then the team; (2) 5-row pushback table with
common objections (Zapier, ChatGPT, security, hallucinations, time)
and specific responses for each.

prompt-injection: add tool-use attack to threat model

Reviewer (Marcus, staff eng): threat model covers exfiltration and
impersonation but misses the most dangerous variant — weaponizing the
agent's own legitimate tool access. A ticket saying 'use Slack to
post to #general' isn't fooling the agent; it's instructing an agent
that already has Slack write access.

Added: explicit tool-use attack example plus explanation of why
narrow write scopes (Mitigation 1) dominate the defense stack for
this class.

TRADEOFFS: add cost scaling scenarios (1x/10x/50x/100x)

Reviewer (Sam, skeptic engineer): cost table shows single-user
estimates with no path for 'what happens when we scale this.' Finance
conversations need the 10x and 100x rows.

Added: 4-row scaling table showing weekly cost at 1x/10x/50x/100x
with the use-case trigger for each scale, plus a $500/week rule of
thumb for when to start caring about cost.

SECURITY: add explicit 'do NOT connect' deny list

Reviewer (Tom, security/IT lead): data flow table describes what we
do connect, nothing about what we explicitly don't. Security teams
need both sides of the line.

Added: 7-item explicit deny list (personal email, admin Slack tokens,
HR Notion workspaces, prod deploy keys, unapproved MCP servers,
confidential Jira projects, customer-facing write tokens).

QUICKSTART: add troubleshooting triage when nothing appears in Slack

Reviewer (Alex, solo startup PM): first Run Now failed silently. Docs
jump straight to 'what you learned' with no recourse for 'what you
actually do when nothing shows up.'

Added: 3-step triage (run log first, DM ID format, connector status)
before the 'what you learned' section.

README: add pre-flight access check per surface

Reviewer (Rohan, senior PM): no way to confirm upfront which surfaces
you can actually use. Free-tier readers waste time reading about
Routines before discovering they need a paid plan.

Added: access check table showing plan/app requirements for each of
the three surfaces, plus where to click to verify you have access.

Add Cowork Scheduled Tasks coverage (2 use cases + folder README)

- New /cowork-tasks/ folder with:
  - README explaining when to pick Cowork over Routines
  - 01-local-transcript-digest: weekly scan of local meeting transcripts
  - 02-morning-brief-to-local-folder: morning brief as local markdown
- README updated to cover 3 surfaces (Cowork + Routines + Managed Agents)
- Decision tree includes Cowork options
- Added 3-surface comparison table
- QUICKSTART mentions Cowork alternative
Update newsletter link to specific post URL

Initial commit: Claude Routines + Managed Agents PM Pack

Companion repo to the newsletter post. 7 production-ready prompts, sample outputs, engineer handoff brief, security + prompt injection docs, 4-week team rollout plan, and measurement framework.
